lines.name: Giuoco Pianissimo
lines.intro: The Giuoco Pianissimo is the slow, strategic Italian. You build a solid center with c3 and d3, castle, and get ready for a d4 break later instead of starting an early fight.

notes.0: Grab the center and open lines for the queen and the f1 bishop.
notes.1: Black mirrors you and claims an equal share of the center.
notes.2: Develop with tempo: the knight attacks e5.
notes.3: Black defends e5 with the knight.
notes.4: The Italian bishop eyes f7, the weakest square in Black's camp.
notes.5: Black copies your idea: this bishop aims at f2, the weak spot next to your king.
notes.6: c3 prepares d4 and opens a retreat path for the bishop via b3–c2.
notes.7: Black develops and attacks your e4 pawn.
notes.8: The quiet d3 keeps e4 solid. This is the slow, maneuvering Pianissimo.
notes.9: Black also plays slowly: ...d6 supports e5 and opens a path for the c8 bishop.
notes.10: Castle. Your king is safe and the rook can come to e1.
notes.12: Re1 supports e4 and gets ready for a later d4 break.
notes.13: Black makes room for the bishop to drop back to a7 and prepares ...b5.
notes.14: Bb3 drops the bishop back before ...b5 or ...d5 can hit it.
notes.15: Black tucks the bishop away on a7, out of reach of a d4 push but still aiming at f2.
notes.16: h3 takes g4 away from Black's knight and bishop.

lines.name: Two Knights, quiet d3
lines.intro: Black plays 3...Nf6 to hit e4 right away. Instead of the sharp 4.Ng5, you calmly defend with d3 and use the same slow plan as the Pianissimo.

notes.0: Grab the center and open lines for the queen and the f1 bishop.
notes.1: Black mirrors you and claims an equal share of the center.
notes.2: Develop with tempo: the knight attacks e5.
notes.3: Black defends e5 with the knight.
notes.4: The Italian bishop eyes f7, the weakest square in Black's camp.
notes.5: This is the Two Knights: Black develops with an attack on your e4 pawn.
notes.6: d3 defends e4 calmly instead of entering the sharp 4.Ng5 lines.
notes.7: Black picks a quiet setup, keeping the bishop at home so it can castle quickly.
notes.8: Castle early. Your king is safe and the rook is coming to e1.
notes.10: Re1 backs up e4 and puts the rook on the file that opens once you play d4.
notes.11: Black supports e5 and frees the c8 bishop.
notes.12: Same plan as the Pianissimo: c3, then d4 when you're ready.

lines.name: vs. Philidor (2...d6)
lines.intro: In the Philidor, Black defends e5 with ...d6, which is solid but passive. You open the center with an early d4 and use your extra space to develop quickly.

notes.0: Grab the center and open lines for the queen and the f1 bishop.
notes.1: Black mirrors you and claims an equal share of the center.
notes.2: Develop with tempo: the knight attacks e5.
notes.3: This is the Philidor: Black defends e5 with a pawn instead of a knight, which shuts in the f8 bishop.
notes.4: Against the passive ...d6, hit the center right away with d4.
notes.5: Black gives up the center instead of holding the tension.
notes.6: Recapture with the knight. It is strong in the center.
notes.9: The bishop goes to e7, its natural square behind the d6 pawn.
notes.10: Be2 is a solid setup that gets ready to castle.
notes.12: Castle. You have more space and an easy game, while Black is solid but cramped.
